questions.q: The letters of the word 'MANKIND' are written in all possible orders and arranged in serial order as in an English dictionary. Then the serial number of the word 'MANKIND' is _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$M$ $A$ $N$ $K$ $I$ $N$ $D$

Arranging the letters alphabetically, we get

ADIKMNN

When the word starts with any of the letters A/D/I/K, the number of possibilities$= \dfrac{6 !}{2 !} \times 4 = 1440$

Now when the word starts with MA, then the number of possibilities$= \dfrac{4 !}{2 !} \times 3 = 36$

Now when the word starts with MAN, then the number of possibilities$= 3 ! \times 2 = 12$

Now when the word starts with MANK, then the number of possibilities$= 4$

Hence, rank of the work MANKIND is~$1492$

questions.q: The number of permutations, of the digits $1, 2, 3, \ldots , 7$ without repetition, which neither contain the string $153$ nor the string $2467$, is _______ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

The number& $1, 2, 3, . . . . , 7$

Now total numbers of~$7$~digit number will be~$7 !$~without repetition,

Now total~numbers which contain string~$154$~will be~$5 !$

Total numbers which contain string~$2367$~will be~$4 !$

And number which contain both string~$2367 \text{ and } 154$~will be~$2$

So, total number which does not contain string~$154$~or~$2367$~will be~$7 ! - \left(5 ! + 4 ! - 2\right)$

$= 5040 - \left(120 + 24 - 2\right)$

$= 5040 - 142 = 4898$

Hence this is the required answer.

questions.q: The total number of two digit numbers $' n '$, such that ${3}^{n} + {7}^{n} \text{ is a multiple of }10$ , is ___ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$∵ {7}^{n} = ( 10 - 3{)}^{n} = 10k + ( - 3{)}^{n}$

${7}^{n} + {3}^{n} = 10k + ( - 3{)}^{n} + {3}^{n}$

$10k + \left(- 3\right)n + \left(3\right)n = \left\{
10kif n=odd
10k + 2 . {3}^{n}if n=even
\right

Let~$n = 2t; t \in N$

$∴ {3}^{n} = {3}^{2t} = ( 10 - 1{)}^{t}$

$= 10p + ( - 1{)}^{t}$

.$= 10p \pm 1$

$∴$ if $n =$ even then ${7}^{n} + {3}^{n}$ will not be multiply of $10$

So if $n$ is odd then only ${7}^{n} + {3}^{n}$ will be multiply of $10$

$∴ n = 11, 13, 15, \ldots \ldots \ldots . , 99$

$∴$ Number of odd two digit numbers $= 45$

questions.q: The number of ways of giving $20$ distinct oranges to $3$ children such that each child gets at least one orange is~_____
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

We have to distribute& $20$~identical~oranges to~$3$~children,

Let children~$A$~get~${O}_{A}$~oranges, children~$B$~gets~${O}_{B}$~oranges and children~$C$~gets~${O}_{C}$~oranges,

So,~${O}_{A} + {O}_{B} + {O}_{C} = 20$

Now this can be distributed using the multinomial theorem,

So, Number of ways will be,

=coefficient of~$x^{20}$~in~\left(x + x^{2} + \ldots . + x^{18}\right)3$

=coefficient of~$x^{20}$~in~$x^{3}\left(1 + x + x^{2} + \ldots . x^{17}\right)3$

=coefficient of~$x^{17}$~in~\left(\dfrac{1 - x^{18}}{1 - x}\right)3$

=coefficient of~$x^{17}$~in~$( 1 - x{)}^{- 3}$

$= C2 19 = 171$

As we know that expansion of~$( 1 - x{)}^{- 3}$~is~$1 + C1 3 x + C2 4 x^{2} + C3 5 x^{3} + . . . . . . + C17 19 x^{17} . . . . . . . . \infty$

Note: This is bonus question as~here $20$& oranges& are considered identical but& in question it is& considered distinct.

questions.q: In an examination, there are& $5$ multiple choice questions with~$3$ choices, out of which exactly one is correct. There are~$3$ marks for each correct answer, $- 2$~marks for each wrong answer and~$0$ mark if the question is not attempted. Then, the number of ways a student appearing in the examination gets~$5$ marks is _____
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the marks obtained in each of the five MCQ be& ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, {x}_{3}, {x}_{4}, {x}_{5}$

Now,~${x}_{1} + {x}_{2} + {x}_{3} + {x}_{4} + {x}_{5} = 5$

Only one possibility satisfies the above equation i.e. $3, 3, 3, - 2, - 2$

Hence, total number of ways $= \dfrac{5 !}{3 ! 2 !} \times 2 \times 2 = 40$

questions.q: The sum of all the elements in the set ${ n \in { 1, 2, \ldots \ldots , 100 } ∣$ H.C.F. of $n$ and $2040$ is 1}& is equal to __________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The prime factorisation of the given number& is& $2040 = {2}^{3} \times 3 \times 5 \times 17$

The H.C.F. of~$n$~and~$2040$~is~$1$~if~$n$~is~not a multiple of $2, 3, 5$~and $17 .$

Hence $n$ cannot be multiple of $2, 3, 5$ and $17$

Then sum is $n ( 1 ) - ( n ( 2 ) + n ( 3 ) + n ( 5 ) + n ( 17 ) - n ( 6 ) - n ( 10 ) - n ( 34 ) - n ( 15 ) - n ( 51 ) - n ( 85 ) ) + n ( 30 ) )$
Where $n ( a )$ means the sum of all numbers belonging to the set ${ 1, 2, \ldots \ldots . 100 }$ which are divisible by~$a$

$= \dfrac{100 \times 101}{2} - \left(\dfrac{2 \times 50 \times 51}{2} + \dfrac{3 \times 33 \times 34}{2} + \dfrac{5 \times 20 \times 21}{2} + \dfrac{17 \times 5 \times 6}{2} - \dfrac{6 \times 16 \times 17}{2} - \dfrac{10 \times 10 \times 11}{2} - \dfrac{34 \times 2 \times 3}{2} - \dfrac{15 \times 6 \times 7}{2} - 51 - 85 + 180\right)$

$= 5050 - 2550 - 1683 - 1050 - 255 + 816 + 550 + 102 + 315 + 51 + 85 - 180$

$= 1251$

Alternate~Solution:
Thus, the sum of all the required numbers taking the common elements only once, is \left(1 + 3 + 5 + \ldots . . + 99\right) - \left(3 + 9 + 15 + 21 + \ldots \ldots + 99\right) - \left(5 + 25 + 35 + 55 + 65 + 85 + 95\right) - \left(17\right)$

Now, using the sum of~$n$~terms of an arithmetic progression i.e.~${S}_{n} = $\dfrac{n}{2}\left[$a + l\right],$~where~$a$~is the first term and~$l$~is the last term.

=\dfrac{50}{2}\left[$1 + 99\right] - $\dfrac{17}{2}\left[$3 + 99\right] - \left(365\right) - 17$

=\dfrac{50}{2}\left($100\right) - $\dfrac{17}{2}\left($102\right) - 365 - 17$

$= 2500 - 867 - 365 - 17$

$= 1251 .$

$

questions.q: Number of integral solutions to the equation $x + y + z = 21$, where $x \ge 1, y \ge 3, z \ge 4$, is equal to _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

$x \ge 1, y \ge 3, z \ge 4$

$⇒ x - 1 \ge 0, y - 3 \ge 0, z - 4 \ge 0$

So,

$x + y + z = 21$

$⇒ \left(x - 1\right) + \left(y - 3\right) + \left(z - 4\right) = 13$

So, number of non-negative integral solutions is

$= C3 - 1 13 + 3 - 1 = C2 15 = \dfrac{15 \times 14}{2} = 105$

questions.q: The number of words, with or without meaning, that can be formed using all the letters of the word ASSASSINATION so that the vowels occur together, is _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
In the word $ASSASSINATION$, we will treat all the vowels that is~$AAAIIO$ ~as one letter only.

Now, we have~\left(AAAIIO\right)SSSSNNT$

This has $8 = ( 7 + 1 )$ letters of which $S$~occurs $4$~times, and $N$~occur $2$~times,

Thus, the number of ways of~ arranging these letters $= \dfrac{8 !}{4 ! 2 !} = 840$.

Now, $6$ vowels in which $A$~occurs $3$times, and $I$~occur two times, they~can be arranged in~$\dfrac{6 !}{3 ! 2 !} = 60\text{ways.}$

~Therefore, required number of ways$= ( 840 \times 60 ) = 50400 .$

$

questions.q: The number of ways,& $16$ identical cubes, of which~$11$ are blue and rest are red, can be placed in a row so that between any two red cubes there should be at least~$2$ blue cubes, is ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,& $4$~blue~& $5$~red spherical~ball

Now according to~question~there should be minimum 2 blue ball in between any two red ball.

So assume~$a, b, c, d, e, f$~are~number of blue balls,

So,~$a + b + c + d + e + f = 11$~......(i)

Where~$b, c, d, e ⩾ 2$

Now let~$b = b^{'} + 2$

$c = c^{'} + 2$

$d = d^{'} + 2$

$e = e^{'} + 2$

So equation (i) becomes

$a + b^{'} + 2 + c^{'} + 2 + d^{'} + 2 + e^{'} + 2 + f = 11$

$⇒ a + b^{'} + c^{'} + d^{'} + e^{'} + f = 3$

Now total ways will be

${=}^{3 + 6 - 1}{C}_{6 - 1}{=}^{8}{C}_{5}{=}^{8}{C}_{3} = 56$

questions.q: If the digits are not allowed to repeat in any number formed by using the digits $0, 2, 4, 6, 8,$ then the number of all numbers greater than $10, 000$& is equal to __________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have to form a number greater than& $10, 000$~by using the digits~$0, 2, 4, 6, 8,$~hence, the first place of the number can't be zero.

Thus, for the first place we have~$4$~choices i.e.~$2, 4, 6, 8$~and the remaining places can be filled with any of the digits, thus~we have respectively~$4, 3, 2, 1$~choices.

Hence, using the fundamental principle of multiplication, the total numbers which are greater than~$10, 000$~are

$= 4 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 = 96 .$

questions.q: Let $S = \left\{1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11\right\}$. The number of non-empty subsets of $S$ that have the sum of all elements a multiple of $3$, is _____ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given set is

$S = \left\{1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 11\right\}$

Elements of the type $3k$~is~$3$.

Elements of the type $3k + 1$~are~\left\{1, 7, 9\right\}$.

Elements of the type $3k + 2$~are~\left\{2, 5, 11\right\}$

Subset~containing one element ${S}_{1} = 1$

Subsets containing two elements~${S}_{2}$~

$= C1 3 \times C1 3 = 9$

Subsets containing three elements~${S}_{3}$

$= C1 3 \times C1 3 + 1 + 1 = 11$

Subsets containing four elements~${S}_{4}$

$= C3 3 + C3 3 + C2 3 \times C2 3 = 11$

Subsets containing five elements~${S}_{5}$

$= C2 3 \times C2 3 \times 1 = 9$

Subsets containing six elements ${S}_{6} = 1$

Subsets containing seven elements~${S}_{7} = 1$

Required number

$= 1 + 9 + 11 + 11 + 9 + 1 + 1$

$= 43$

questions.q: The number of seven digit positive integers formed using the digits $1, 2, 3$ and $4$~only and sum of the digits equal to $12$ is_______ .
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given numbers are& $1, 2, 3, 4$~and sum of digits should be~$12$.

Case~$1: 4 3 1 1 1 1 1$~,Here the sum of the digits is~$12$.

The number of ways arranging them is~$= \dfrac{7 !}{5 !} = 42$.

Case~$2: 4 2 2 1 1 1 1$.

The number of ways arranging them is~$= \dfrac{7 !}{2 ! 4 !} = 105$

Case~$3: 3 2 2 2 1 1 1$.

The number of ways arranging them is~$= \dfrac{7 !}{3 ! 3 !} = 140$

Case~$4: 3 3 2 1 1 1 1$.

The number of ways arranging them is~$= \dfrac{7 !}{2 ! 4 !} = 105$

Case~$5: 2 2 2 2 2 1 1$

The number of ways arranging them is~$= \dfrac{7 !}{5 ! 2 !} = 21$

The total number of ways are~$= 42 + 105 + 140 + 105 + 21$

$= 413$

Therefore, the required answer is~$413$.
